parsed.headline: Voters head to the polls for Toronto’s 2026 municipal election

pages.text: Voters in Toronto, Canada, are scheduled to head to the polls on October 17, 2026, for the municipal election. According to the City of Toronto, voting places on election day will be open from 10 a.m. to 8 p.m. While voting places close at 8 p.m., any voter in line by that time will be permitted to vote. To avoid lineups, officials suggest considering voting during off-peak hours between 11 a.m. and 3 p.m.  To vote in person, individuals must show one piece of acceptable identification that includes their name and a qualifying Toronto address; photo identification is not required. Voters are also encouraged to bring a paper or digital Voter Information Card (VIC) to expedite the process. Eligible voters must vote at their assigned voting place as indicated on their VIC or the Toronto Elections webpage. To be eligible to vote, a person must vote in the ward where they live, and may only vote once regardless of how many properties they own or rent in Toronto.

parsed.headline: New research programme launched to strengthen West Africa outbreak response

pages.text: A new regional initiative, the Africa Research Preparedness Programme for West Africa, has been launched to strengthen preparedness for public health emergencies by connecting research institutions and enabling coordinated responses to disease outbreaks. The programme aims to address gaps in research coordination that experts say can delay critical interventions during outbreaks of diseases such as Ebola, Mpox, Lassa fever, and COVID-19. While skilled scientists and established research institutions exist across the continent, preparedness remains uneven, with some clinical trial sites facing challenges transitioning from routine research to emergency response. Shingai Machingaidze, Head of Africa Strategy and Engagement at the Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations (CEPI), stated the programme will adopt a hub-and-spoke model to connect existing research capabilities. This approach is intended to allow countries to work together on research protocols and evidence generation, with the goal of activating clinical research responses within 10 to 15 days of an outbreak.

The initiative brings together several organizations involved in public health research, regulation, and outbreak preparedness, including the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC), the African Medicines Agency, the World Health Organization’s Regional Office for Africa, the Noguchi Memorial Institute for Medical Research, the Medical Research Council Unit The Gambia, the International Vaccine Institute (IVI), and CEPI. The collaboration is intended to provide a common platform for institutions across West Africa to align priorities, share expertise, and strengthen emergency research systems so that institutions can mobilize resources rather than working in isolation. Birkneh Tadesse, Associate Director-General of the International Vaccine Institute in South Korea, noted that operational research and clinical trials are important to efforts to develop vaccines and support responses to outbreaks, including Ebola.

parsed.headline: Alberta voters reject constitutional amendments in 10-part referendum

pages.text: In a 10-part referendum held in Alberta, Canada, voters rejected all four questions regarding whether the province should pursue constitutional amendments. According to CBC Canada, the results included a rejection of a question about abolishing the Senate, which did not receive a simple majority of votes. Alberta Premier Danielle Smith noted at a news conference on October 21, 2026, that the results on immigration questions differed from the results on constitutional questions, suggesting voters may prefer to focus on areas where meaningful change can be made. Smith stated on October 20, 2026, that not every grievance Alberta has with Ottawa has been resolved and that political and constitutional battles remain ahead.

Regarding the province's status within Canada, 75 per cent of voters chose the first option to remain in the country, a result described as more decisive than the 1980 referendum in Quebec. While 25 per cent of voters opted for another referendum, Abacus Data reported that making Alberta an independent country was the primary motivation for only 32 per cent of those who favored the second option.

parsed.headline: Former law adviser expresses hope for constitutional reform committee in Bangladesh

pages.text: Professor Asif Nazrul, a former law adviser to the interim government in Bangladesh, stated that he hopes the parliamentary committee on constitutional reform will deliver the largest possible gains, even if the results fall short of the sweeping changes originally envisioned under the interim administration. Nazrul, who served under the interim government led by Nobel laureate Muhammad Yunus, expressed a desire for a constitution more advanced than the current version, noting that any positive change constitutes a reform. He stated that while the aim is to achieve the maximum possible progress, any achievement will be considered a gain. The July National Charter was previously adopted for state reform under the Yunus-led interim government. Following opposition street protests demanding the implementation of the Charter, the BNP government formed the current committee. While the committee has met with political parties, alliances, academics, teachers, eminent citizens, social and professional group leaders, women leaders, and stakeholders of the July Uprising, the opposition has sent no representatives.

The committee's ninth meeting was held at the parliament complex, presided over by Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed and attended by legal experts. During a meeting on Saturday, legal experts provided views regarding the drafting of a widely acceptable amendment, overall reform, and the strengthening of constitutional institutions. Previous efforts to form a Constitution Reform Council in accordance with a referendum verdict encountered difficulties at the beginning. Following the February 12 election, winners from the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) took oaths only as MPs, whereas winners from the Jamaat-e-Islami-led alliance took oaths for both roles.

parsed.headline: Ghanaian economist proposes African Reserve Unit to address intra-African trade costs

pages.text: Henry Bruce, a Ghanaian economist and commodity trader, has proposed the creation of the African Reserve Unit (ARU) as a solution to the complexities of continental trade. Bruce, who has approximately 22 years of experience trading diesel and petrol in West African markets and has worked in central banking, argues that the solution to trade challenges is not another digital currency. He suggests that much of the current focus on digital money involves fiat money moving faster on new rails, but that a faster system does not change the underlying reliance on external reserves to settle trade. Bruce notes that a dollar on a phone remains a dollar, and Africa continues to depend on the reserves of others to facilitate transactions. This proposal comes amid observations that intra-African trade is commonly estimated at around 15 per cent of the continent's total, partly due to the high costs associated with payment processes. He cites examples where a buyer in Accra holding cedis must pay a seller wanting dollars through banks in New York or London to settle trades, such as diesel shipments bound for Tema.

parsed.headline: Criminal activity and attacks on River Police rise across Bangladesh waterways

pages.text: River-related crimes and attacks on law enforcement are increasing across the 11 regions monitored by the River Police in Bangladesh, according to senior River Police officials. Reported activities include murder, robbery, kidnapping, piracy, extortion, drug smuggling, and illegal sand extraction. Officials told Prothom Alo that criminals are increasingly utilizing river routes because law enforcement surveillance is less extensive on the water than on land. Criminal activities have been reported on various vessels, including passenger trawlers, fishing boats, cargo vessels, and bulkheads. Boat workers have reportedly been beaten or hacked with machetes for refusing to pay extortion, while cargo vessels have been looted of goods such as fertilizer. Members of the River Police have also come under attack while conducting operations to prevent these crimes.

Data regarding filed cases shows a significant increase in reported incidents. In 2024, 2,085 cases were filed involving murder, unnatural deaths, robbery, snatching, weapons, transportation of stolen goods, illegal sand extraction, kidnapping, extortion, and drug-related offences. In 2025, the number of cases rose to 3,399, an increase of 1,314 from the previous year. Between January and September of this year, an additional 505 cases were filed involving murder, robbery, kidnapping, piracy, and unnatural deaths. Combined, these figures represent a total of 5,989 cases recorded over the specified periods. In a specific incident on the night of 1 February last year, a 30-year-old fisherman named Md. Hossain was killed by pirate gunfire while fishing in the Meghna River near East Ilisha union in Bhola Sadar upazila; three other fishermen, identified as Abbas, Kanchan, and Sohel, were injured in the shooting.

parsed.headline: Three sitting councillors compete for Oshawa mayoralty in upcoming municipal election

pages.text: Three sitting councillors are vying to replace outgoing Oshawa Mayor Dan Carter in the municipal election scheduled for Oct. 26 in Oshawa, Canada. Candidates include Ward 2 regional and city councillor Tito-Dante Marimpietri, city councillor Jim Lee, and Derek Giberson. 10. CBC Toronto reports that Marimpietri intends to grow the city's commercial and industrial tax base by attracting new businesses and investment to reduce the burden on residents. He has pledged to develop a budget framework to keep municipal tax increases at or below the rate of inflation and plans to review budget pressures, discretionary spending, and reserves for savings opportunities within his first 100 days in office. Jim Lee has also pledged to hold property tax increases at the rate of inflation. Derek Giberson stated that while municipal and regional governments have fewer tools than provincial and federal governments to address affordability, they can make a difference through housing. Giberson's focus is on delivering more affordable non-profit housing units to reduce the cost of living. He also supports maintaining free public services, such as libraries, while keeping paid programs affordable and offering reduced fees to those in need.
